headline: India, Pakistan summon diplomats after naval collision in international waters
summary: Naval vessels from India and Pakistan collided in international waters, prompting both nuclear-armed nations to lodge strong protests with each other's top diplomats. This marks the first overt military tension since last year's conflict.
details: India and Pakistan have summoned each other's top diplomats to lodge strong protests following a collision between their naval vessels in international waters. Both nations accused the other of "unacceptable and unprofessional conduct" or "highly provocative action."

This incident represents the first overt military tension between the nuclear-armed neighbours since a fierce, four-day military conflict last year. That previous conflict had raised fears of a wider war before a ceasefire was eventually reached.

Indian sources claim the collision occurred when a Pakistani naval ship moved too close to a frontline Indian warship on a routine surveillance mission in the north Arabian Sea. Conversely, Pakistan's foreign ministry stated that the Indian vessel carried out "aggressive manoeuvres in dangerously close proximity" to a Pakistani naval ship participating in biennial exercises.

The impact did not cause any major damage, but India highlighted that Pakistan's conduct was "in direct contravention" of a 1991 agreement. This agreement mandates that naval ships and submarines of the two countries maintain a distance of at least three nautical miles from each other to prevent accidents in international waters.

Both foreign ministries advised their respective diplomats to convey to the concerned authorities the need to observe due care and respect existing agreements to prevent any repeat of such incidents. India and Pakistan have downgraded their diplomatic relations since 2019 over the Kashmir dispute, with their missions now headed by a charge d'affaires.

The arch-rivals have engaged in three major wars, two of which were over Kashmir, which is divided between them but claimed in full by both. Numerous armed skirmishes have also occurred since their independence from British colonial India in 1947.

headline: Houthis launch drone and missile attacks on Saudi cities, including near Mecca, as Yemen conflict spreads
summary: The conflict between Saudi Arabia and Houthi fighters has intensified, with Houthi forces launching drones and missiles at Saudi cities and Saudi warplanes pounding Yemen. This escalation includes an alleged Houthi drone targeting Mecca, which Saudi Arabia cla
details: Houthi fighters launched drones and missiles at Saudi cities, while Saudi warplanes pounded Yemen. This escalation follows a Houthi advance that has extended Iran's reach in the Middle East conflict.

Saudi Arabia reported intercepting a Houthi drone south of Mecca on Tuesday, preventing it from entering the holy city's airspace. Riyadh called this an attack that crossed a "red line" for threatening shrines sacred to Muslims, though Houthi spokesmen denied targeting Mecca.

Houthi military spokesman Yahya Saree claimed fresh drone and missile strikes on the major Saudi Red Sea oil port of Yanbu and a southern Saudi airbase at Khamis Mushait. He also stated that Houthis had shot down a Saudi F-15 fighter jet, though no immediate evidence was presented.

The United States has tightened its travel warning for Saudi Arabia, banning government employees from traveling within 20 miles of the Yemen border. This highlights the worsening conflict and its regional implications.

The conflict had largely quieted under a ceasefire in recent years but reignited when Houthis declared a naval blockade against Saudi Arabia in July. Violence intensified this month as the militant group pushed back forces aligned with the Saudi-backed Yemeni government.

An attack last week, blamed on Iran-aligned fighters in Iraq, also disrupted Saudi Arabia's East-West Pipeline, a crucial route for oil exports. Traders warn that a prolonged closure could cut off up to 4% of global oil supply.

Brent crude prices are hovering around $108 a barrel, near their highest levels since May, and US diesel fuel prices hit an all-time high. The extension of the war threatens to worsen the global energy supply shortage caused by the ongoing US-Israeli war on Iran.
